newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Engen volumes high on foreign sales.
newsitem.headline: Engen volumes high on foreign sales.

text.p: Volumes in South African oils group Engen Ltd swelled on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Tuesday morning as foreigners sold stock to local buyers, dealers said.
By 0948 GMT almost two million Engen shares worth 42.0 million rand hand changed hands, making it one of the most active by volume on the bourse. The stock was last at 21.25 rand, 25 cents down.

Dealers said the bulk of the trade was in two large deals done by brokerage SBC Warburg, which last week pushed almost two billion rands worth of stocks offshore in dealings which probably represented an entire portfolio being moved overseas.
"If you ask me it looks like it is some of the stock Warburgs sent out last week coming back into the country," one dealer said.

With the introduction of a new feature-enhanced trading system on Monday, JSE dealers can now distinguish between foreign purchases and sales. Previously a blanket "foreign trade" code was ascribed to all offshore deals.
